newsitem.title: AUSTRIA: Italy's Prodi "deeply worried" over Albania.
newsitem.headline: Italy's Prodi "deeply worried" over Albania.

text.p: Italian Prime Minister Romano Prodi expressed grave concern on Friday over a rift between Albania's political parties which may endanger plans to hold a a general election slated for June 29.
"I express my really deep, deep worry," Prodi told reporters after talks with Austrian Chancellor Viktor Klima.
Prodi and Klima said they believed it would be difficult for Europe to continue to help Albania if the parties failed to reach consensus on election procedures.
The two leaders echoed a similar statement by the Organisation for Security and Cooperation in Europe (OSCE).

"Failure to achieve agreement could lead the OSCE and others to reconsider their commitment to assist Albania in overcoming the country's present crisis," the OSCE's current chairman Danish Foreign Minister Niels Helvig Petersen said.
Italy is leading a multinational military force to protect aid supplies in Albania.

Asked if Rome would withdraw the mission in the event of a serious political breakdown, Prodi said: "Of course this is not a decision we want to take, but the multinational force went in to build up something new and we have to consider in the case of no agreement if our mission will still be fruitful."

Albanian President Sali Berisha on Friday called the early elections for June 29, although most political parties are threatening to boycott them. They say an electoral law favours Berisha's Democratic Party.
The West views elections as vital to resolving the crisis in Albania, which descended into anarchy after thousands of people lost their life savings in pyramid investment schemes.
"We must give a clear statement that agreement is the only way of making a real start in the reconstruction of Albania. This must be based on democracy and transparent elections," Prodi noted.
The Italian premier said the framework already existed for an agreement but needed fine tuning, adding he would be talking to Albanian political leaders at the weekend.

The OSCE special envoy to Albania Franz Vranitzky on Thursday appeared to have brokered a fresh deal to get the polls back on track but opposition parties on Friday indicated the new election law was still not acceptable.
Prodi said the Albania mission had been tricky from the start but that European intervention had prevented a repeat of the Yugoslav conflict.
"I think the mission was very important. I think we avoided civil war," he said.
